result.markdown: --- title: "Discrete-event simulation" course-unit: a03-discrete-event-simulation status: complete --- ## Why this unit matters - Jump-process chapter: aggregate counts, "what happens next, to how many?" - Agent-based chapter: individuals, but a fixed time step $\Delta t = 0.1$. - Discrete-event simulation (DES): individuals **and** a continuous clock — jump directly from one scheduled event to the next, no discretization. - Built two ways here: Agents.jl's `EventQueueABM`, and the general-purpose, process-oriented `ConcurrentSim.jl`. ::: {.notes} Position this as the synthesis unit: same underlying CTMC as the jump-process chapter, but resolved per individual, which is what lets it express a fixed delay directly — no history function required. ::: ## Model assumptions and classification Usual baseline: $N=1000$, $S(0)=990$, $I(0)=10$, $R(0)=0$, $c=10$, $\beta=0.05$, $\gamma=0.25$. Each individual's next contact and recovery are scheduled as events; the clock jumps to the next event anywhere in the population. | Property | Classification | |---|---| | Determinism | Stochastic | | Time | Continuous, event-driven (no fixed $\Delta t$) | | State | Discrete (individual status) | | Representation | Individual-level | ## Equations $$ T_\text{contact} \sim \mathrm{Exponential}(1/c), \qquad \Pr(\text{infect} \mid \text{contact w/ infectious}) = \beta $$ $$ T_\text{recovery} \sim \mathrm{Exponential}(1/\gamma) $$ By memorylessness and superposition of independent Poisson processes, the *population-level* counting process is exactly the jump-process CTMC; the event-queue view additionally retains *who* infected *whom* and *when*. ## Julia API: `EventQueueABM` ```julia using Agents @agent struct Person(NoSpaceAgent) status::Symbol end transmit_propensity(a, m) = a.status == :S ? m.c : 0.0 recovery_propensity(a, m) = a.status == :I ? m.γ : 0.0 events = (AgentEvent(action! = transmit!, propensity = transmit_propensity), AgentEvent(action! = recover!, propensity = recovery_propensity)) model = EventQueueABM(Person, events; properties, rng) run!(model, tf; adata = [(:status, infected)]) ``` By default an `AgentEvent`'s `timing` samples an exponential wait parameterized by its `propensity` — matching the equations above exactly. ## Julia API: `ConcurrentSim.jl` ```julia using ConcurrentSim, ResumableFunctions @resumable function live(sim, person, m, rng) while person.status == :S @yield timeout(sim, rand(rng, Exponential(1 / m.c))) alter = rand(rng, m.people) alter.status == :I && rand(rng) < m.β && (person.status = :I) end if person.status == :I @yield timeout(sim, rand(rng, Exponential(1 / m.γ))) person.status = :R end end ``` Not agent-centric: coroutine `@resumable` processes plus `Resource`/`Store` primitives for queueing and contention — more bookkeeping, more generality. ## Generated result ::: {#cell-fig-slide-a03-trajectories .cell execution_count=1} ::: {#fig-slide-a03-trajectories .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Single EventQueueABM and ConcurrentSim realisations against the deterministic ODE mean field. ::: ::: ## Validation - **Conservation**: every recorded row of both simulations sums to $N$. - **Monotonicity**: the one-way $S \to I \to R$ transition keeps $S$ non-increasing and $R$ non-decreasing in both implementations. - **Ensemble check**: a 20-run `EventQueueABM` ensemble's mean final size is within 10% of the deterministic ODE prediction. ## Interpretation and limitations - `EventQueueABM` automates scheduling but its default `adata` samples once per unit time — coarser than the true event resolution. - `ConcurrentSim` needs hand-written recording, but every event is captured exactly when it happens, and its `Resource`/`Store` primitives extend to models with no natural agent-centric analogue (e.g. limited hospital beds). - Both scale worse than the aggregated jump-process CTMC: scheduling $O(N)$ individual events costs more than resampling one aggregate draw. - Neither requires exponential timing: `AgentEvent`'s `timing` and `ConcurrentSim`'s `timeout` both accept arbitrary — including fixed — waiting times, so a DES can encode the fixed delay of the DDE unit directly, with no history function or method of steps. ::: {.notes} The fixed-delay exercise is the payoff line connecting this unit back to the very first appendix: individual-level bookkeeping sidesteps the whole history-function machinery because each agent just remembers its own infection time. ::: ## Key takeaways - DES resolves the same CTMC as the jump-process chapter, per individual, on a continuous event-driven clock. - `EventQueueABM` (Agents.jl 7) and `ConcurrentSim.jl` are two current, complementary ways to build one: agent/event-centric vs. general process/resource-centric. - A DES can express fixed delays and resource contention that are awkward or impossible in the population-level or fixed-$\Delta t$ models earlier in the course. ## Further reading - [Agents.jl `EventQueueABM` documentation](https://juliadynamics.github.io/Agents.jl/stable/api/#Agents.EventQueueABM) - [ConcurrentSim.jl repository](https://github.com/JuliaDynamics/ConcurrentSim.jl) - Full derivation, code, and exercises: [book chapter](../../appendices/03-discrete-event-simulation.html)
